source.title: Military Intelligence Branch officer career pamphlet, DA PAM 600-3 chapter (August 2026)
source.proponent: U.S. Army Intelligence Center of Excellence (MI proponent)
source.notes: Date basis: the PDF prints only 'AUG2026'; 2026-08-06 is the upload date in the official URL path (…/2026/08/06/…). Imported for 35A, 35B: the grade-by-grade development sections (O-1..O-2, O-3, O-4, O-5, O-6) as the pamphlet gives them for the branch or functional area; they apply to every AOC listed. Duties and prerequisites are not imported from this pamphlet (DA PAM 611-21 is the source); figures and tables are not extracted. The second run of grade headings (page 22 on) is the Reserve Component text and is not imported. passages.heading: Lieutenant development — Education
passages.chapter: Military Intelligence Branch officer career pamphlet, DA PAM 600-3 chapter (August 2026)
passages.body: Successful completion of the Military Intelligence Basic Officer Leader Course (BOLC) at the U.S. Army Intelligence Center of Excellence at Fort Huachuca, AZ.

passages.heading: Lieutenant development — Assignment
passages.chapter: Military Intelligence Branch officer career pamphlet, DA PAM 600-3 chapter (August 2026)
passages.body: After completing Military Intelligence BOLC, Human Resources Command will likely assign Military Intelligence lieutenants to serve in leadership developmental positions such as platoon leader, company executive officer (XO), assistant battalion S2, combat support battalion S2, assistant brigade S2, or staff officer in a Military Intelligence organization. Military Intelligence lieutenants most commonly serve as intelligence officers at echelons of corps and below. Lieutenants should strive to acquire, reinforce, and hone troop-leading, tactical, technical, logistics, and administrative skills. Inculcation of the Army Values and the Warrior Ethos is essential in the development of Military Intelligence lieutenants. Prior to promotion to captain, the officer must possess an in-depth knowledge of combined arms and intelligence operations gained through operational experiences.

passages.heading: Lieutenant development — Additional guidance
passages.chapter: Military Intelligence Branch officer career pamphlet, DA PAM 600-3 chapter (August 2026)
passages.body: The Military Intelligence Branch Detail Program is an important part of the Military Intelligence officer accession process. This critical program assigns newly commissioned officers to branches with large lieutenant requirements. It exposes a large number of operations support officers to operations branches. Upon selection for promotion to captain, these officers become Military Intelligence officers and are scheduled for MI OTC prior to attending the MI CCC. MI OTC attendance is limited to active component officers. After completing both courses, leaders develop detailed officers in the same manner as their non-detailed Military Intelligence counterparts.

passages.heading: Lieutenant development — Self-development
passages.chapter: Military Intelligence Branch officer career pamphlet, DA PAM 600-3 chapter (August 2026)
passages.body: Lieutenants should take every opportunity to broaden their knowledge of all aspects of military intelligence through studying doctrine, professional readings, and personal research.

passages.heading: Captain development — Education
passages.chapter: Military Intelligence Branch officer career pamphlet, DA PAM 600-3 chapter (August 2026)
passages.body: Successful completion of the Military Intelligence CCC.

passages.heading: Captain development — Key Developmental (KD) assignments
passages.chapter: Military Intelligence Branch officer career pamphlet, DA PAM 600-3 chapter (August 2026)
passages.body:
KD complete for Military Intelligence Captains is service of at least 12 months in one of the following KD assignments:
(a) Battalion/Squadron S2
(b) Company/Security Forces Assistance Brigade (SFAB) Company/Detachment Commander
(c) Brigade/Regiment/Group Assistant S2
(d) Target Officer

passages.heading: Captain development — Broadening assignments
passages.chapter: Military Intelligence Branch officer career pamphlet, DA PAM 600-3 chapter (August 2026)
passages.body: In addition to the KD assignments listed above, MI captains may serve in additional or successive KD positions to strengthen their leadership, tactical, and technical skills for career development. Following successful KD assignments, Military Intelligence officers should attempt to gain maximum experience by serving in a variety of Military Intelligence duty positions. Branch-specific assignments will provide captains with exposure to the Army and, in some cases, to Joint, Interagency, Intergovernmental, and Multinational (JIIM) organizations.

passages.heading: Captain development — Self-development
passages.chapter: Military Intelligence Branch officer career pamphlet, DA PAM 600-3 chapter (August 2026)
passages.body: Military Intelligence captains should take every opportunity to broaden their knowledge of all aspects of the Army and military intelligence through studying doctrine, reviewing professional readings, and completing personal research into intelligence related topics.

passages.heading: Major development — Education
passages.chapter: Military Intelligence Branch officer career pamphlet, DA PAM 600-3 chapter (August 2026)
passages.body: Successful completion of Intermediate Level Education (ILE)/Joint Professional Military Education (JPME) I level producing course. Refer to AR 611-21 for more information on the required PME. After selection for 35B, officers have 24 months to complete required PME. Commanding General, U.S. Army Intelligence Center of Excellence is the sole waiver authority.

passages.heading: Major development — Key developmental assignments
passages.chapter: Military Intelligence Branch officer career pamphlet, DA PAM 600-3 chapter (August 2026)
passages.body: All 35B assignments are KD for AOC 35B Strategic Intelligence majors. These positions consist of reoccurring assignments at theater, national, DOD, joint and interagency communities. These are positions in which 35Bs integrate interagency intelligence activities and conduct strategic intelligence planning, collection, and analysis that require the application of strategic skills, regional/functional expertise, and deep knowledge of the national intelligence community.

passages.heading: Major development — Additional guidance
passages.chapter: Military Intelligence Branch officer career pamphlet, DA PAM 600-3 chapter (August 2026)
passages.body:
The following are KD assignments for Military Intelligence (AOC 35A) majors:
(a) Brigade/ Regiment/ Group S2
(b) Battalion/Brigade/Group S3 or XO
(c) Division/Multi-Domain Task Force (MDTF) Analysis and Control Element (ACE) Chief
(d) Deputy G2 Division and higher
(e) Collection Manager
(f) Special Mission Unit (SMU) Troop Commander
(g) Corps/Division Intel Planner (SAMS utilization only)

passages.heading: Major development — Broadening assignments
passages.chapter: Military Intelligence Branch officer career pamphlet, DA PAM 600-3 chapter (August 2026)
passages.body: Military Intelligence majors should strive to have a broad base of intelligence experience at various echelons. Following their successful KD assignment(s), MI majors should serve in a balance of division, echelon at or above corps, and joint assignments. Experience at multiple echelons will assist Military Intelligence majors at the next rank.

passages.heading: Major development — Self-development
passages.chapter: Military Intelligence Branch officer career pamphlet, DA PAM 600-3 chapter (August 2026)
passages.body: Majors should actively pursue self-development opportunities to fully master all aspects of operations including tactical and JIIM operations. Self-development includes studying doctrine, correspondence courses, civilian education, and institutional training. Military Intelligence majors should consider publication in academic and professional journals, as it will encourage Military Intelligence majors to critically develop their thoughts for a wide and discriminating audience.

passages.heading: Lieutenant Colonel development — Education
passages.chapter: Military Intelligence Branch officer career pamphlet, DA PAM 600-3 chapter (August 2026)
passages.body: Military Intelligence lieutenant colonels are encouraged to complete JPMEII.

passages.heading: Lieutenant Colonel development — Key developmental assignments
passages.chapter: Military Intelligence Branch officer career pamphlet, DA PAM 600-3 chapter (August 2026)
passages.body: All 35B assignments are KD for 35B lieutenant colonels. These positions consist of more intelligence managerial assignments across the theater, national, joint, and interagency communities. At this echelon, 35Bs direct and synchronize interagency intelligence activities overseeing the strategic intelligence planning, collection, and analysis apparatus.

passages.heading: Lieutenant Colonel development — Additional guidance
passages.chapter: Military Intelligence Branch officer career pamphlet, DA PAM 600-3 chapter (August 2026)
passages.body:
The following are KD assignments for 35A Military Intelligence lieutenant colonels, including any assignment identified on the Centralized Selection List – Key Billet (CSL-KB) Slate:
(a) Division/Multi-Domain Task Force (MDTF) G2
(b) Battalion Commander
(c) Corps or higher ACE Chief / JISE Chief

passages.heading: Lieutenant Colonel development — Broadening assignments
passages.chapter: Military Intelligence Branch officer career pamphlet, DA PAM 600-3 chapter (August 2026)
passages.body: Officers selected for lieutenant colonel and CSL positions must seek assignments within the branch that directly contribute to and develop the Army intelligence profession. Lieutenant colonels serve at multiple echelons and types of positions throughout their career. Lieutenant colonels should seek the opportunity for joint qualification and intelligence broadening assignments.

passages.heading: Lieutenant Colonel development — Self-development
passages.chapter: Military Intelligence Branch officer career pamphlet, DA PAM 600-3 chapter (August 2026)
passages.body: Lieutenant colonels must actively pursue self-development opportunities to fully master aspects of operations including continued performance at multiple echelons.

passages.heading: Colonel development — Education
passages.chapter: Military Intelligence Branch officer career pamphlet, DA PAM 600-3 chapter (August 2026)
passages.body: Successful completion of a JPME II certificate through the Senior Service College (SSC) or the successful completion of a JPME II level producing course.

passages.heading: Colonel development — Key developmental assignments
passages.chapter: Military Intelligence Branch officer career pamphlet, DA PAM 600-3 chapter (August 2026)
passages.body: All 35B assignments are KD for 35B colonels. . These positions consist of JIOC Commanders, National Agency and CCMD Division Chiefs, and Branch Heads. At this echelon, 35Bs lead strategic intelligence organizations and direct comprehensive global intelligence portfolios. They apply regional, functional, and institutional mastery to govern multi-agency intelligence architectures and synchronize complex intelligence activities.

passages.heading: Colonel development — Additional guidance
passages.chapter: Military Intelligence Branch officer career pamphlet, DA PAM 600-3 chapter (August 2026)
passages.body:
35A Colonels contribute to the branch by serving in critical KD assignments, including any assignment identified on the Centralized Selection List – Key Billet (CSL-KB):
(a) Corps G2
(b) Brigade Commander
(c) Transformation & Lessons Learned Integrator (TLLM) (former ACM)
(d) Army Service Component Command / Army Command or higher G2/J2
(e) Chief of Staff

passages.heading: Colonel development — Broadening assignments
passages.chapter: Military Intelligence Branch officer career pamphlet, DA PAM 600-3 chapter (August 2026)
passages.body: Officers selected for colonel and CSL positions must seek assignments that directly contribute to and develop the Army intelligence profession.
